formulation.rationale: The group contains one canonical heparin product. ASGE distinguishes intravenous from subcutaneous UFH timing, so those distinctions are preserved as recommendation qualifiers rather than collapsed.

sources.title: The management of antithrombotic agents for patients undergoing GI endoscopy

passages.quote: UFH | IV 2-6 hours / SQ 12-24 hours | Hold | Protamine sulfate (partial)
UFH administered intravenously has a half-life of 60 to 90 minutes, and anticoagulant effects dissipate 3 to 4 hours after discontinuation.

passages.locator: Reinitiation of antithrombotic agents after elective endoscopy
passages.quote: There is consensus that antithrombotic therapy should be resumed upon completion of the procedure.

passages.locator: Reinitiation of antithrombotic agents after elective endoscopy
passages.quote: UFH may be restarted 2 to 6 hours after a therapeutic procedure.

comparisons.checked_locators: Table 2; Parenteral and subcutaneously administered anticoagulants; Reinitiation of antithrombotic agents after elective endoscopy
comparisons.note: ASGE explicitly addresses elective UFH holding, preserves different IV and SQ durations of action, and provides a UFH restart interval after therapeutic procedures.

recommendations.applicability: Elective GI endoscopy in a patient receiving intravenous UFH.
recommendations.exceptions: Table 2 labels 2-6 hours as duration of action; this package does not reinterpret that number as a separately stated mandatory interruption interval.
recommendations.summary: ASGE Table 2 says to hold elective intravenous UFH and lists an IV duration of action of 2-6 hours.

recommendations.applicability: Elective GI endoscopy in a patient receiving subcutaneous UFH.
recommendations.exceptions: Table 2 labels 12-24 hours as duration of action; this package does not reinterpret that number as a separately stated mandatory interruption interval.
recommendations.summary: ASGE Table 2 says to hold elective subcutaneous UFH and lists an SQ duration of action of 12-24 hours.

recommendations.applicability: Day of elective GI endoscopy when the patient is receiving intravenous UFH.
recommendations.exceptions: Route must be known because ASGE lists different IV and SQ durations.
recommendations.summary: ASGE identifies elective intravenous UFH as a drug to hold and lists an IV duration of action of 2-6 hours.

recommendations.applicability: Day of elective GI endoscopy when the patient is receiving subcutaneous UFH.
recommendations.exceptions: Route must be known because ASGE lists different IV and SQ durations.
recommendations.summary: ASGE identifies elective subcutaneous UFH as a drug to hold and lists an SQ duration of action of 12-24 hours.

recommendations.timing_text: resumed upon completion of the procedure
recommendations.applicability: General ASGE statement for resumption of antithrombotic therapy after elective endoscopy.
recommendations.exceptions: Immediate reinitiation must be balanced against agent- and procedure-specific hemorrhage risk; ASGE separately specifies UFH after therapeutic procedures.
recommendations.summary: ASGE states that antithrombotic therapy should be resumed upon completion of the procedure.

recommendations.resume_text: UFH may be restarted 2 to 6 hours after a therapeutic procedure.
recommendations.applicability: UFH after a therapeutic GI endoscopic procedure.
recommendations.exceptions: The statement is specific to therapeutic procedures and uses 'may be restarted'; adequate hemostasis and procedure-specific bleeding risk remain relevant.
recommendations.summary: ASGE says UFH may be restarted 2 to 6 hours after a therapeutic procedure.

scenario_coverage.reason: ASGE Table 2 addresses elective UFH holding with separate IV and SQ durations.
ASGE Table 2 identifies elective UFH as Hold, with route-specific duration-of-action information.
ASGE provides a general resumption statement and a UFH-specific 2-6 hour restart statement after therapeutic procedures.

open_questions.text: The canonical MED-heparin record does not specify route, while ASGE distinguishes IV from SQ UFH. The clinician should apply the qualifier matching the actual product/route.
The ASGE HTML exposes the exact restart-section quotes but not their print page number; the package therefore records the section locator and flags the page field rather than guessing a page.

editorial.notes: Unreviewed evidence package. Route-specific distinctions are intentionally preserved; Table 2 duration-of-action values are not presented as if ASGE explicitly labeled them mandatory hold intervals.
